problem: Language understanding for human-robot navigation dialogue (ScoutBot) was handled by a relevance-based classifier, and it was unclear how a fine-tuned generative LM compares and what kinds of errors each makes. Prior error analysis only used coarse correct/close/wrong categories.
motivation: Robots must translate free-form commander instructions into restricted executable commands, and wrong executions are costly, whereas asking for rephrasing is safe. Understanding the distinct error profiles of a classification model and a generative model could allow combining them to get better accuracy.
key_idea: Compare an NPCEditor relevance-based classifier with a fine-tuned GPT-2 on ~2000 examples for instruction-to-command translation, introduce a 7-way error taxonomy, and test model combinations.
insight: With about 2k training examples the classifier (79.23%) beats GPT-2 (68.31%), but errors differ: GPT-2 makes genuine errors (37% vs 10%) and hallucinations, while NPCEditor makes more numerical (24% vs 7%) and no-response errors. Oracle combination reaches 84.69% and a simple routing rule (numeric utterances to GPT-2, rest to NPCEditor) reaches 79.78%, so complementarity exists but is hard to exploit. A learning-curve on full/half/quarter data shows GPT-2 improving with more data.
method: NPCEditor classifier: statistical language model per response class, cross-language relevance for ranking a canned simplified-command output, with a confidence threshold that allows No Response
GPT-2 Medium fine-tuning: 24 layers, 16 heads, 325M params, trained 25 epochs on 'directive [SEP] cmd1 [CSEP] cmd2 [EOS]' sequences, decoded with top-k/nucleus sampling and beam search
Error taxonomy: Genuine, Hallucination, No Response, Contextual, Numerical, Directional, Felicitous; each of 183 test items manually labeled for both models
Confusion matrix between models' error categories showing overlap (Contextual, Directional shared; Hallucination only GPT-2, No Response only NPCEditor)
Oracle combination: picks the correct output of the two per item as upper bound
Decision-level combination: routes utterances containing numbers to GPT-2, all others to NPCEditor

setting.backbone: NPCEditor (statistical relevance classifier, trained) and GPT-2 Medium (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: 2058 annotated user utterances (493 system responses, 2153 links) from ScoutBot Wizard-of-Oz human-robot dialogue; earlier 966-utterance set for the prior baseline
setting.action_space: text-to-simplified-command translation (e.g. 'turn to face west then move forward fifteen feet')
setting.simulator: none (offline text evaluation on ScoutBot corpus)

numbers_note: Only text-command accuracy on a 183-item ScoutBot test set, not a canonical navigation benchmark: NPCEditor 79.23%, Gervits et al. 2021 75.41%, GPT-2 68.31%, Oracle 84.69%, decision-level combination 79.78%.
results: NPCEditor reached 79.23% accuracy vs 68.31% for fine-tuned GPT-2 on 183 test instructions, improving over the prior 75.41%. Oracle combination gives 84.69% and a numeric-routing combination 79.78%.
limitations: Small training set (~2k) and small test set (183), so GPT-2 is likely undertrained and conclusions may not generalize
Evaluation is text-only exact matching of commands with no actual robot or environment; contextual errors are unresolved
Combination is only a heuristic routing rule with gain ~0.5 points over the NPCEditor
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
